note: Neither cross-check is a hypothesis test. Both are reported descriptively per the plan's own instruction to report them 'separately as a cherry-picked set'.

crosscheck_1_trading_journal.method: Queried all rows, then filtered to trades dated on a Monday within the study window (2026-05-11 to 2026-11-09).
crosscheck_1_trading_journal.detail: 11 rows returned total: 3 blank/placeholder rows, and 8 real logged trades (RCT, INO x2, DBGI, CENN x2, VSA, VIVK). Every one of the 8 real trades is dated 2026-11-06, which is a Friday, not a Monday. None fall inside the pre-registered Monday-only study window.
crosscheck_1_trading_journal.conclusion: Caleb's journal has no Monday trades in the study window to grade against the four checks. This is reported as-is rather than papered over; it means cross-check 1 contributes no evidence either way on H1-H5.

crosscheck_2_newsletter_runners.source: Tim Sykes newsletter email, 2026-10-24, naming 5 Monday runners with self-reported % moves
crosscheck_2_newsletter_runners.limitation_sample_size: n=5 is far below the plan's 10-per-group insufficient-data threshold. No Mann-Whitney/Holm/regression test is run on this set; it is reported only as a cherry-picked table, per the plan's Task 7 instruction.
crosscheck_2_newsletter_runners.limitation_catalyst: Catalyst was not blind-labeled for this set (no separate labeling subagent dispatch was run for 5 items). WORX/MI/SOAR show catalyst as 'not_labeled'. MNDR and GRML are reused directly from the main pipeline's graded.csv, where MNDR's catalyst was 'catalyst_excluded' (no pre-open news found) and GRML's catalyst was 'True'.
crosscheck_2_newsletter_runners.limitation_pct_mismatch: The newsletter's self-reported % moves do not match this study's pre-registered outcome metric (max gain from the open = high/open - 1 on the daily bar). The newsletter figures are plausibly measured from a different, lower baseline (e.g. multi-day or close-to-close) and are NOT directly comparable to max_gain below. Both are shown so the mismatch is visible rather than silently reconciled.

crosscheck_2_newsletter_runners.descriptive_summary: All 5 named runners pass low_float and stale_float is mixed (3 of 5 flagged stale). unusual_volume passes 3/5 (WORX, MNDR, GRML); former_runner passes only 1/5 (SOAR). Of the 2 rows with a labeled catalyst, GRML had one and MNDR did not (excluded). This small, cherry-picked set shows the same qualitative pattern as the main n=301 sample (unusual_volume and low_float are the most commonly-passing checks; former_runner is the rarest), but with n=5 and no catalyst label on 3/5 rows this is not evidence for or against any hypothesis -- consistent with, not independent confirmation of, the main finding.
crosscheck_2_newsletter_runners.conclusion: Reported descriptively only, as the plan requires. No H1-H5 verdict is affected by this cross-check.
